title: Slack Water
audience: adult literary readers who like grounded, character-driven realism and craft
reader_contract: strictly linear: one morning, first light to the top of the tide; no flashback, no framing device
a concrete problem with a clear physical cause and a clear, earned turn
sensory, plainspoken prose; feeling is carried by the work of the hands and the read of the wood, not named
a quiet, legible ending: recognition, not triumph; the customer does not hand over tidy thanks
theme_question: When is it truer to let a made thing be finished than to force it to work?
desired_affect: the steadiness of telling the truth about the work
constraints: events happen in the order the reader receives them; no gimmick structure
no coincidence-rescue; the turn comes from Rennie's competence and judgment
prose earns feeling through concrete action; no told emotion, no cliche, no adverbial dialogue tags
Aldous is grief-driven, not a villain, and does not deliver tidy validation
the launching is honest, not a trick: everyone present knows the boat is not sound
